newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.

text.p: * World Bank President James Wolfensohn, visiting Romania, met Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea.

The radio quoted Wolfensohn as saying that the World Bank would give Romania loans worth $600 million in 1997. The money would come from a second tranche of the Financial and Enterprise Structural Adjustment Loan (FESAL), a new Agriculture Structural Adjustment Loan (ASAL) and from a social welfare project loan as the country restrung standards in rural areas of Romania, the radio quoted Wolfensohn as saying.
* Wolfensohn hailed the government's progresses in recent months in reforming Romanian economy.

* Romanian-Moldovan ties go beyond simple bilateral links, taking into account the two country's common history, Moldovan Prime Minister Ion Ciubuc told the state news agency Rompres ahead of his visit to Romania on Thursday.
* The parliament's upper chamber, the Senate, resumed its sessions on Monday.
* MPs of the opposition Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) slammed a draft law by the ruling coalition to ease procedures to lift parliamentary immunity.
* Romania liberalised its exports of grain starting Monday, following moves by the government to cut subsidies to the farming sector, the industry ministry said.
* The Romanian troops on the multi-national mission in Albania were put under Italian command in the town of Gjirokaster on Monday. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
